questions.question_en: If log_2(x) + log_4(x) + log_16(x) = 7, then the value of x is:
questions.question_hi:
[Quantitative Aptitude (Logarithms) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
If log_2(x) + log_4(x) + log_16(x) = 7, then the value of x is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
Using change of base to base 2: log_2(x) + (1/2)log_2(x) + (1/4)log_2(x) = (7/4)log_2(x) = 7 => log_2(x) = 4 => x = 2⁴ = 16.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Using change of base to base 2: log_2(x) + (1/2)log_2(x) + (1/4)log_2(x) = (7/4)log_2(x) = 7 => log_2(x) = 4 => x = 2⁴ = 16.

questions.question_en: A radioactive detector records an average of 2 cosmic-ray muons per minute following a Poisson distribution. The probability that zero muons are detected in a 2-minute interval is:
questions.question_hi:
[Probability (Poisson Process) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A radioactive detector records an average of 2 cosmic-ray muons per minute following a Poisson distribution. The probability that zero muons are detected in a 2-minute interval is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
For a 2-minute interval, the mean count is λ = 2 × 2 = 4. The Poisson probability of k = 0 events is P(0) = e^(−λ) λ⁰ / 0! = e^(−4).
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
For a 2-minute interval, the mean count is λ = 2 × 2 = 4. The Poisson probability of k = 0 events is P(0) = e^(−λ) λ⁰ / 0! = e^(−4).

questions.question_en: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small right circular cones, each of radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. The number of cones formed is:

questions.question_en: The residue of the complex function f(z) = cot(z) = cos(z)/sin(z) at its simple pole z = π is:

The residue of the complex function f(z) = cot(z) = cos(z)/sin(z) at its simple pole z = π is:

For f(z) = g(z)/h(z) with g(π) = cos(π) = −1 and h'(π) = cos(π) = −1, the residue at the simple pole z = π is g(π)/h'(π) = (−1)/(−1) = 1.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):

questions.question_en: The value of the definite integral ∫_{−∞}^{∞} (x² + 3x + 5) δ(x − 2) dx, where δ(x) is the Dirac delta distribution, is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Mathematical Physics (Fourier Transform & Dirac Delta) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
The value of the definite integral ∫_{−∞}^{∞} (x² + 3x + 5) δ(x − 2) dx, where δ(x) is the Dirac delta distribution, is ________.
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
By the sifting property of the Dirac delta function, ∫ f(x) δ(x − a) dx = f(a). At a = 2, f(2) = 2² + 3(2) + 5 = 4 + 6 + 5 = 15.

questions.question_en: A particle of mass m moves in one dimension under the Hamiltonian H(q, p) = p²/(2m) + k q⁴ (where k > 0). According to the Virial Theorem, the relation between the time-averaged kinetic energy ⟨T⟩ and time-averaged potential energy ⟨V⟩ for a bound periodic orbit is:
questions.question_hi:
[Classical Mechanics (Hamiltonian Dynamics) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A particle of mass m moves in one dimension under the Hamiltonian H(q, p) = p²/(2m) + k q⁴ (where k > 0). According to the Virial Theorem, the relation between the time-averaged kinetic energy ⟨T⟩ and time-averaged potential energy ⟨V⟩ for a bound periodic orbit is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
For a homogeneous potential V(q) = k q^n, the Virial Theorem states 2⟨T⟩ = n⟨V⟩. Here n = 4, so 2⟨T⟩ = 4⟨V⟩ => ⟨T⟩ = 2⟨V⟩.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
For a homogeneous potential V(q) = k q^n, the Virial Theorem states 2⟨T⟩ = n⟨V⟩. Here n = 4, so 2⟨T⟩ = 4⟨V⟩ => ⟨T⟩ = 2⟨V⟩.

questions.question_en: If q and p are canonical coordinate and momentum variables satisfying {q, p} = 1, then the canonical transformation Q = q^α cos(β p), P = q^α sin(β p) preserves the fundamental Poisson bracket {Q, P} = 1 if (α, β) are:
questions.question_hi:
[Classical Mechanics (Poisson Brackets) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
If q and p are canonical coordinate and momentum variables satisfying {q, p} = 1, then the canonical transformation Q = q^α cos(β p), P = q^α sin(β p) preserves the fundamental Poisson bracket {Q, P} = 1 if (α, β) are:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
{Q, P} = (∂Q/∂q)(∂P/∂p) − (∂Q/∂p)(∂P/∂q) = [α q^(α−1) cos(βp)][β q^α cos(βp)] − [−β q^α sin(βp)][α q^(α−1) sin(βp)] = α β q^(2α−1). Setting this equal to 1 for all q requires 2α − 1 = 0 => α = 1/2, and α β = 1 => β = 2.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
{Q, P} = (∂Q/∂q)(∂P/∂p) − (∂Q/∂p)(∂P/∂q) = [α q^(α−1) cos(βp)][β q^α cos(βp)] − [−β q^α sin(βp)][α q^(α−1) sin(βp)] = α β q^(2α−1). Setting this equal to 1 for all q requires 2α − 1 = 0 => α = 1/2, and α β = 1 => β = 2.

questions.question_en: A relativistic unstable particle of rest mass m0 decays at rest into two identical particles each of rest mass m0 / 4. The speed of each daughter particle in units of c (rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Classical Mechanics (Special Relativity) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A relativistic unstable particle of rest mass m0 decays at rest into two identical particles each of rest mass m0 / 4. The speed of each daughter particle in units of c (rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
By conservation of energy and momentum, the two identical daughter particles fly apart with equal energy E = m0 c² / 2. Since E = γ m_d c² = γ (m0/4) c², we have γ = 2. From γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) = 2 => 1 − v²/c² = 1/4 => v/c = √3 / 2 ≈ 0.866.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
By conservation of energy and momentum, the two identical daughter particles fly apart with equal energy E = m0 c² / 2. Since E = γ m_d c² = γ (m0/4) c², we have γ = 2. From γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) = 2 => 1 − v²/c² = 1/4 => v/c = √3 / 2 ≈ 0.866.

questions.question_en: Four point charges are placed in the xy-plane: +q at (a, 0), +q at (−a, 0), −q at (0, a), and −q at (0, −a). At large distances r >> a, the electrostatic potential V(r) falls off with distance r as:
questions.question_hi:
[Electromagnetic Theory (Multipole Expansion) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Four point charges are placed in the xy-plane: +q at (a, 0), +q at (−a, 0), −q at (0, a), and −q at (0, −a). At large distances r >> a, the electrostatic potential V(r) falls off with distance r as:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
Total monopole charge Q = +q + q − q − q = 0. Total dipole moment p⃗ = q(a x̂ − a x̂ − a ŷ + a ŷ) = 0⃗. The quadrupole tensor Q_{ij} is non-zero (Q_{xx} = 4qa², Q_{yy} = −4qa²), so V(r) ∝ 1/r³.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Total monopole charge Q = +q + q − q − q = 0. Total dipole moment p⃗ = q(a x̂ − a x̂ − a ŷ + a ŷ) = 0⃗. The quadrupole tensor Q_{ij} is non-zero (Q_{xx} = 4qa², Q_{yy} = −4qa²), so V(r) ∝ 1/r³.

questions.question_en: A rectangular hollow metallic waveguide has cross-sectional dimensions a = 4 cm and b = 2 cm (with a > b). The cutoff frequency f_c for the dominant TE_{10} mode in free space (c = 3 × 10¹⁰ cm/s) is:

A rectangular hollow metallic waveguide has cross-sectional dimensions a = 4 cm and b = 2 cm (with a > b). The cutoff frequency f_c for the dominant TE_{10} mode in free space (c = 3 × 10¹⁰ cm/s) is:

For the dominant TE_{10} mode (m=1, n=0), the cutoff wavelength is λ_c = 2a = 8 cm, so the cutoff frequency is f_c = c / (2a) = (3 × 10¹⁰ cm/s) / (8 cm) = 3.75 × 10⁹ Hz = 3.75 GHz.

questions.question_en: For a monochromatic plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum with electric field E⃗(r⃗, t) = E0 x̂ cos(kz − ωt), which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
[Electromagnetic Theory (Maxwell's Equations & Poynting Vector) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
For a monochromatic plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum with electric field E⃗(r⃗, t) = E0 x̂ cos(kz − ωt), which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
options_en: The magnetic field is B⃗(r⃗, t) = (E0 / c) ŷ cos(kz − ωt).
The time-averaged Poynting vector is ⟨S⃗⟩ = (1/2) ε0 c E0² ẑ.
The electric energy density equals the magnetic energy density at every instant.
The wave carries a net longitudinal electric field component along ẑ.
options_hi: The magnetic field is B⃗(r⃗, t) = (E0 / c) ŷ cos(kz − ωt).
The time-averaged Poynting vector is ⟨S⃗⟩ = (1/2) ε0 c E0² ẑ.
The electric energy density equals the magnetic energy density at every instant.
The wave carries a net longitudinal electric field component along ẑ.
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
In vacuum, B⃗ = (k̂ × E⃗)/c = (ẑ × x̂)(E0/c) cos(kz − ωt) = (E0/c) ŷ cos(kz − ωt). The electric and magnetic energy densities u_E = (1/2)ε0 E² and u_B = B²/(2μ0) are identically equal, and ⟨S⃗⟩ = (1/2) ε0 c E0² ẑ.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
In vacuum, B⃗ = (k̂ × E⃗)/c = (ẑ × x̂)(E0/c) cos(kz − ωt) = (E0/c) ŷ cos(kz − ωt). The electric and magnetic energy densities u_E = (1/2)ε0 E² and u_B = B²/(2μ0) are identically equal, and ⟨S⃗⟩ = (1/2) ε0 c E0² ẑ.

questions.question_en: A 1D quantum harmonic oscillator of angular frequency ω is prepared in the normalized state |ψ(0)⟩ = (1/√2)(|0⟩ + |1⟩), where |n⟩ are the energy eigenstates with E_n = (n + 1/2)ℏω. The expectation value of energy ⟨H⟩ in this state is:

A 1D quantum harmonic oscillator of angular frequency ω is prepared in the normalized state |ψ(0)⟩ = (1/√2)(|0⟩ + |1⟩), where |n⟩ are the energy eigenstates with E_n = (n + 1/2)ℏω. The expectation value of energy ⟨H⟩ in this state is:

questions.question_en: A particle of mass m in a 1D infinite potential well 0 ≤ x ≤ L (with V = 0 inside) is subjected to a localized delta perturbation H' = α δ(x − L/2). The first-order correction E_n^(1) to the energy of the n-th state is:
questions.question_hi:
[Quantum Mechanics (First-Order Perturbation Theory) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A particle of mass m in a 1D infinite potential well 0 ≤ x ≤ L (with V = 0 inside) is subjected to a localized delta perturbation H' = α δ(x − L/2). The first-order correction E_n^(1) to the energy of the n-th state is:
options_en: (2α / L) for odd n, and 0 for even n
(2α / L) for even n, and 0 for odd n
options_hi: (2α / L) for odd n, and 0 for even n
(2α / L) for even n, and 0 for odd n
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
The unperturbed eigenstates are ψ_n(x) = √(2/L) sin(nπx/L). Thus E_n^(1) = ⟨ψ_n|H'|ψ_n⟩ = α |ψ_n(L/2)|² = (2α/L) sin²(nπ/2), which equals 2α/L for odd n and 0 for even n (since even states have a node at x = L/2).
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
The unperturbed eigenstates are ψ_n(x) = √(2/L) sin(nπx/L). Thus E_n^(1) = ⟨ψ_n|H'|ψ_n⟩ = α |ψ_n(L/2)|² = (2α/L) sin²(nπ/2), which equals 2α/L for odd n and 0 for even n (since even states have a node at x = L/2).

questions.question_en: Let L⃗ = (L_x, L_y, L_z) be the orbital angular momentum operator of a quantum particle. Which of the following commutation relation(s) is/are TRUE?
questions.question_hi:
[Quantum Mechanics (Angular Momentum Algebra) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Let L⃗ = (L_x, L_y, L_z) be the orbital angular momentum operator of a quantum particle. Which of the following commutation relation(s) is/are TRUE?
options_en: [L_z, L_+] = ℏ L_+ (where L_+ = L_x + i L_y)
options_hi: [L_z, L_+] = ℏ L_+ (where L_+ = L_x + i L_y)
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
L² is a Casimir invariant of SO(3) and commutes with all components L_x, L_y, L_z (so [L², L_z] = 0 and [L_x, L²] = 0). The fundamental commutator is [L_x, L_y] = iℏL_z, and for the raising operator L_+, [L_z, L_+] = ℏL_+.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
L² is a Casimir invariant of SO(3) and commutes with all components L_x, L_y, L_z (so [L², L_z] = 0 and [L_x, L²] = 0). The fundamental commutator is [L_x, L_y] = iℏL_z, and for the raising operator L_+, [L_z, L_+] = ℏL_+.

questions.question_en: Using the thermodynamic fundamental relation dG = −S dT + V dP for the Gibbs free energy G(T, P), the Maxwell relation is:
questions.question_hi:
[Thermodynamics (Maxwell Relations) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Using the thermodynamic fundamental relation dG = −S dT + V dP for the Gibbs free energy G(T, P), the Maxwell relation is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
Since dG = −S dT + V dP is an exact differential, equality of mixed partial derivatives ∂²G/(∂P ∂T) = ∂²G/(∂T ∂P) yields −(∂S/∂P)_T = (∂V/∂T)_P, or (∂S/∂P)_T = −(∂V/∂T)_P.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since dG = −S dT + V dP is an exact differential, equality of mixed partial derivatives ∂²G/(∂P ∂T) = ∂²G/(∂T ∂P) yields −(∂S/∂P)_T = (∂V/∂T)_P, or (∂S/∂P)_T = −(∂V/∂T)_P.

questions.question_en: A system of N non-interacting, distinguishable spin-like particles has two single-particle energy levels: ε_0 = 0 (non-degenerate) and ε_1 = ε (doubly degenerate, g_1 = 2). At temperature T (with β = 1/(k_B T)), the canonical partition function Z_N and the high-temperature limit (T → ∞) of the mean energy ⟨E⟩ are:
questions.question_hi:
[Statistical Physics (Two-Level Partition Function) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A system of N non-interacting, distinguishable spin-like particles has two single-particle energy levels: ε_0 = 0 (non-degenerate) and ε_1 = ε (doubly degenerate, g_1 = 2). At temperature T (with β = 1/(k_B T)), the canonical partition function Z_N and the high-temperature limit (T → ∞) of the mean energy ⟨E⟩ are:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
Single-particle partition function z_1 = 1·e^0 + 2·e^(−βε) = 1 + 2e^(−βε), so Z_N = (z_1)^N = (1 + 2e^(−βε))^N. Mean energy ⟨E⟩ = N (2ε e^(−βε)) / (1 + 2e^(−βε)). As T → ∞ (β → 0), e^(−βε) → 1, so ⟨E⟩ → (2/3) N ε.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Single-particle partition function z_1 = 1·e^0 + 2·e^(−βε) = 1 + 2e^(−βε), so Z_N = (z_1)^N = (1 + 2e^(−βε))^N. Mean energy ⟨E⟩ = N (2ε e^(−βε)) / (1 + 2e^(−βε)). As T → ∞ (β → 0), e^(−βε) → 1, so ⟨E⟩ → (2/3) N ε.

questions.question_en: For a 3D degenerate gas of ultra-relativistic spin-1/2 fermions (dispersion relation ε = p c) at T = 0 K, the Fermi energy E_F scales with particle number density n as E_F ∝ n^α. The value of the exponent α (rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Statistical Physics (Relativistic Fermi Gas) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
For a 3D degenerate gas of ultra-relativistic spin-1/2 fermions (dispersion relation ε = p c) at T = 0 K, the Fermi energy E_F scales with particle number density n as E_F ∝ n^α. The value of the exponent α (rounded to two decimal places) is ________.
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
In 3D, the Fermi wavevector k_F = (3π² n)^(1/3) ∝ n^(1/3). For ultra-relativistic fermions, E_F = ℏ c k_F ∝ n^(1/3), so α = 1/3 ≈ 0.33.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
In 3D, the Fermi wavevector k_F = (3π² n)^(1/3) ∝ n^(1/3). For ultra-relativistic fermions, E_F = ℏ c k_F ∝ n^(1/3), so α = 1/3 ≈ 0.33.

questions.question_en: According to Hund's rules, the ground-state spectroscopic term symbol of a neutral Carbon atom (1s² 2s² 2p²) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Atomic Physics (L-S Coupling Ground State) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
According to Hund's rules, the ground-state spectroscopic term symbol of a neutral Carbon atom (1s² 2s² 2p²) is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
For two equivalent p-electrons (2p², less than half-filled): maximum spin S = 1 (2S+1 = 3), maximum orbital angular momentum consistent with Pauli exclusion L = 1 (P state), and since the subshell is less than half-filled, minimum J = |L − S| = |1 − 1| = 0. Thus the ground state is ³P_0.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
For two equivalent p-electrons (2p², less than half-filled): maximum spin S = 1 (2S+1 = 3), maximum orbital angular momentum consistent with Pauli exclusion L = 1 (P state), and since the subshell is less than half-filled, minimum J = |L − S| = |1 − 1| = 0. Thus the ground state is ³P_0.

questions.question_en: In the pure rotational Raman spectrum of a homonuclear diatomic rigid rotor with rotational constant B (in cm⁻¹), the wavenumber separation between the first Stokes line (J = 0 → 2) and the first anti-Stokes line (J = 2 → 0) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Molecular Spectroscopy (Rotational Raman) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In the pure rotational Raman spectrum of a homonuclear diatomic rigid rotor with rotational constant B (in cm⁻¹), the wavenumber separation between the first Stokes line (J = 0 → 2) and the first anti-Stokes line (J = 2 → 0) is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
For rotational Raman scattering (selection rule ΔJ = ±2), the shift from the Rayleigh line is |Δν̃| = B(4J + 6). For J = 0, the first Stokes line is at ν̃_0 − 6B and the first anti-Stokes line is at ν̃_0 + 6B. The separation between them is 6B − (−6B) = 12B.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
For rotational Raman scattering (selection rule ΔJ = ±2), the shift from the Rayleigh line is |Δν̃| = B(4J + 6). For J = 0, the first Stokes line is at ν̃_0 − 6B and the first anti-Stokes line is at ν̃_0 + 6B. The separation between them is 6B − (−6B) = 12B.

questions.question_en: The Atomic Packing Factor (APF) of a diamond cubic crystal structure (such as Silicon or Germanium) expressed as a percentage (rounded to the nearest integer, given √3 π / 16 ≈ 0.3401) is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Solid State Physics (Atomic Packing Factor) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
The Atomic Packing Factor (APF) of a diamond cubic crystal structure (such as Silicon or Germanium) expressed as a percentage (rounded to the nearest integer, given √3 π / 16 ≈ 0.3401) is ________.
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
In the diamond cubic lattice (8 atoms per unit cell, nearest-neighbor distance d = √3 a / 4 = 2r), APF = 8 × (4/3)π r³ / a³ = √3 π / 16 ≈ 0.3401 = 34%.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
In the diamond cubic lattice (8 atoms per unit cell, nearest-neighbor distance d = √3 a / 4 = 2r), APF = 8 × (4/3)π r³ / a³ = √3 π / 16 ≈ 0.3401 = 34%.

questions.question_en: An ideal operational amplifier is connected in a non-inverting amplifier configuration with input resistor R1 = 2 kΩ connected from the inverting terminal (−) to ground and feedback resistor R_f = 18 kΩ connected from the output to the inverting terminal (−). The closed-loop voltage gain A_v = V_out / V_in is:
questions.question_hi:
[Electronics (Operational Amplifiers) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
An ideal operational amplifier is connected in a non-inverting amplifier configuration with input resistor R1 = 2 kΩ connected from the inverting terminal (−) to ground and feedback resistor R_f = 18 kΩ connected from the output to the inverting terminal (−). The closed-loop voltage gain A_v = V_out / V_in is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
For an ideal non-inverting op-amp configuration, the closed-loop voltage gain is A_v = 1 + (R_f / R1) = 1 + (18 kΩ / 2 kΩ) = 1 + 9 = 10.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
For an ideal non-inverting op-amp configuration, the closed-loop voltage gain is A_v = 1 + (R_f / R1) = 1 + (18 kΩ / 2 kΩ) = 1 + 9 = 10.

questions.question_en: A 4-bit ripple (asynchronous) binary counter constructed using 4 negative-edge-triggered JK flip-flops (with J = K = 1) is driven by a 32 MHz clock signal. The output frequency (in MHz) at the MSB (Q3) flip-flop is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Digital Electronics (Flip-Flop Frequency Division) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
A 4-bit ripple (asynchronous) binary counter constructed using 4 negative-edge-triggered JK flip-flops (with J = K = 1) is driven by a 32 MHz clock signal. The output frequency (in MHz) at the MSB (Q3) flip-flop is ________.
questions.explanation_en:

An N-stage binary ripple counter divides the input clock frequency by 2^N. For N = 4 flip-flops, f_out = f_clk / 2⁴ = 32 MHz / 16 = 2.0 MHz.

questions.question_en: In the nuclear single-particle shell model with spin-orbit coupling, the ground-state spin and parity (J^π) of the ¹⁷O nucleus (Z = 8, N = 9) is:
questions.question_hi:
[Nuclear Physics (Single-Particle Shell Model) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In the nuclear single-particle shell model with spin-orbit coupling, the ground-state spin and parity (J^π) of the ¹⁷O nucleus (Z = 8, N = 9) is:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
In ¹⁷O, the 8 protons and first 8 neutrons fill the closed magic shells (1s_{1/2})² (1p_{3/2})⁴ (1p_{1/2})² (N = Z = 8). The 9th unpaired neutron enters the next available orbital, 1d_{5/2} (l = 2, even parity π = (−1)² = +), giving J^π = (5/2)+.
questions.explanation_hi:

questions.question_en: Which of the following elementary particle reactions/decays is/are ALLOWED by conservation of charge, baryon number, lepton numbers, and energy-momentum?
questions.question_hi:
[Particle Physics (Conservation Laws & Decays) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
Which of the following elementary particle reactions/decays is/are ALLOWED by conservation of charge, baryon number, lepton numbers, and energy-momentum?
options_en: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e (Beta minus decay)
p → e⁺ + γ (Proton decay in Standard Model)
options_hi: n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e (Beta minus decay)
p → e⁺ + γ (Proton decay in Standard Model)
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e, π⁺ → μ⁺ + ν_μ, and μ⁻ → e⁻ + ν̄_e + ν_μ all conserve electric charge Q, baryon number B, and flavor lepton numbers L_e, L_μ. Proton decay p → e⁺ + γ violates baryon number (ΔB = −1) and lepton number (ΔL_e = −1) and is forbidden in the Standard Model.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e, π⁺ → μ⁺ + ν_μ, and μ⁻ → e⁻ + ν̄_e + ν_μ all conserve electric charge Q, baryon number B, and flavor lepton numbers L_e, L_μ. Proton decay p → e⁺ + γ violates baryon number (ΔB = −1) and lepton number (ΔL_e = −1) and is forbidden in the Standard Model.

questions.question_en: In the SU(3) quark model, given that the up quark has electric charge q_u = +2/3 e and the strange quark has electric charge q_s = −1/3 e, the magnitude of the electric charge (in units of e) of the Ω⁻ (sss) baryon is ________.
questions.question_hi:
[Particle Physics (Quark Model Charge) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
In the SU(3) quark model, given that the up quark has electric charge q_u = +2/3 e and the strange quark has electric charge q_s = −1/3 e, the magnitude of the electric charge (in units of e) of the Ω⁻ (sss) baryon is ________.
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
The Ω⁻ baryon consists of three strange quarks (sss), each of charge −1/3 e. Total charge Q = 3 × (−1/3 e) = −1 e, so its magnitude is 1.

questions.question_en: According to the London theory of superconductivity, if the superconducting electron number density n_s decreases by a factor of 4 as temperature approaches T_c, the London penetration depth λ_L = √[m / (μ0 n_s e²)] changes by a factor of:
questions.question_hi:
[Solid State Physics (London Penetration & Superconductivity) • GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024]
According to the London theory of superconductivity, if the superconducting electron number density n_s decreases by a factor of 4 as temperature approaches T_c, the London penetration depth λ_L = √[m / (μ0 n_s e²)] changes by a factor of:
questions.explanation_en:
STEP-BY-STEP DERIVATION:
Since λ_L ∝ n_s^(−1/2), when n_s decreases to n_s / 4, the penetration depth increases by a factor of (1/4)^(−1/2) = 2.
questions.explanation_hi:
चरणबद्ध हल:
आधिकारिक समाधान (GATE Physics (PH) • Feb 2024):
Since λ_L ∝ n_s^(−1/2), when n_s decreases to n_s / 4, the penetration depth increases by a factor of (1/4)^(−1/2) = 2.
